steps.title: Start with the quadratic formula
steps.say: For ax² + bx + c = 0, the formula gives x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a. Here the discriminant is 25 − 24 = 1, so the roots are (5 ± 1) / 2.

steps.title: Switch to factoring
steps.say: The discriminant is a perfect square, so factoring is quicker. I erase the formula work and look for two numbers with product 6 and sum −5.

ops.text: Find p, q:  p · q = 6,  p + q = −5

steps.title: Factor the quadratic
steps.say: Those two numbers let us write the quadratic as a product of two binomials.

steps.title: Use the zero-product property
steps.say: If a product equals zero, at least one factor must be zero. Set each factor to zero.

steps.title: Read off the solutions
steps.say: Solving each linear equation gives the two roots, x = 2 and x = 3.

steps.title: Check both roots
steps.say: Substitute each root back into the original equation. Both give 0, so the solutions are correct.
